title: Splitting a nodal curve point over a finite separable field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $C_\Omega=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change] is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and at every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] its maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For every point $x\in C$ at which $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth, $x$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points], $\kappa(x)/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and there is a finite separable field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] containing a chosen copy of $\kappa(x)$, with $[k':\kappa(x)]\leq2$, and a $k'$-rational point $x'\in C_{k'}$ above $x$ such that $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_{k'},x'}\cong k'[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as $k'$-algebras. Here $k'$-rational means that the induced residue-field map $k'\to\kappa(x')$ is an isomorphism; the last condition is called a split node.

source.place: Tags 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), 0CBW (lemma-split-node); applied to the nodal points characterized by lemma-nodal, as in the residue-field paragraph of lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family.

proof.text: Put $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. Since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal), $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian, and [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. The geometric-fibre hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] are precisely the hypotheses here: geometric points of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are algebraically closed extensions $\Omega/k$. Apply that node. With $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], it says $|Z|$ is the nonsmooth locus, $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified, and these closed subschemes and their supports commute with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, residue-field paragraph; Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family)

proof.text: The prescribed nonsmooth point $x$ belongs to $Z$. The morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type: on a finite-type affine chart of $C$, its ring is the quotient of the chart ring by the first Fitting ideal. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] to $Z$. It gives that $x$ is closed in $Z$, $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=\kappa_Z(x)$, and $F=\kappa_Z(x)$ is finite separable over $k$. A closed subscheme has the same residue field as the ambient scheme at each of its points: on an affine chart both residues are the fraction field of $A/\mathfrak p$. Thus $F=\kappa_C(x)$. Since $Z$ is closed in $C$, closedness in $Z$ implies closedness in $C$. This proves the first assertions, without assuming at the outset that $x$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, second paragraph; Morphisms Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field)

proof.text: Let $D=C_F$ and let $z\in D$ be induced by the residue-point map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to C$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. On an affine chart this is the surjection $A\otimes_kF\to F$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto a(x)\lambda$, so $z$ is $F$-rational and lies over $x$. The residue-point map factors through $Z$, since its defining ideal is contained in the prime of $x$. Hence $z\in Z_F$. Step 1, including its support assertion after base change, makes $z$ nonsmooth on $D$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$. The induced $\Omega$-rational point $\bar z$ belongs to $Z_\Omega$ and is nonsmooth on $D_\Omega=C_\Omega$; the hypothesis therefore identifies its completed local ring with $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. These constructions use only the fibre-product universal property and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

source.place: Tag 0CBY, residue-field paragraph; rationalization of the nodal fibre point

proof.text: Check the dimension needed for the rational-node normal-form lemma. The finitely many affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $C$ base change to charts of $D$ with rings $A_i\otimes_kF$, finitely generated over $F$ by the images of the generators of $A_i$; thus $D$ is of finite type. Their base changes to $\Omega$ are a cover of $D_\Omega=C_\Omega$. Apply the ring assertion of [lem-pc-dim-base-change] to each of the finite-type $F$-algebras $A_i\otimes_kF$, and take suprema over the two covers by [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover]. The identification with topological dimension is [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]. It gives $\dim D=\dim C_\Omega=1$: the latter scheme is nonempty because it has $\bar z$, and all its irreducible components have dimension one by hypothesis. The affine identifications are [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Finally $z$ is closed in $D$. Indeed on any affine open containing it the evaluation map to $F$ is onto, so its prime is maximal; if a point specializes from $z$, an affine neighbourhood of that point contains $z$, and maximality forces that specialization to equal $z$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D hypotheses; dimension under extension of the ground field, Algebra Tag 00P3

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-node-quadratic-completion] over $F$ to $D,z$. Step 3 gives the geometric completed equation, and step 4 gives dimension one, local finite type, and closedness; $F\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism by step 3. Obtain an $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,z}\cong F[[u,v]]/(q)$, where $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ and $\Delta=b^2-4ac\ne0$. The coefficients and the $F$-algebra structure are the ones supplied by this isomorphism; no noncanonical identification of the ground field with another residue subfield is made.

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal) and 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), residue field equal to F

proof.text:
Construct a field $K/F$ of degree at most two. If $a=0$, then $b
e0$, and take $K=F$. If $a
e0$, put $p(T)=aT^2+bT+c$. If $p$ has a root $r\in F$, again take $K=F$. Otherwise $p$ is irreducible (a reducible quadratic has a linear factor), and take the field $K=F[T]/(p)$, with $r$ the class of $T$. The coefficient map embeds $F$, and division by $p$ gives the basis $1,r$, so $[K:F]=2$. This extension is separable: when $2
e0$, a common root of $p$ and $p'=2aT+b$ would force $\Delta=0$ by $(2aT+b)^2-4ap=\Delta$; in characteristic two, $p'=b
e0$. Every element is $s+tr$; for $t
e0$ it satisfies the quadratic $t^2p((T-s)/t)$, whose discriminant is $t^2\Delta
e0$, and for $t=0$ it lies in $F$. Its minimal polynomial divides that separable polynomial, so it is separable. This proves separability from its definition [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], including characteristic two.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), explicit quadratic algebra, and the two cases in Tag 0CBY

proof.text: The quadratic splits into two independent linear forms over $K$. If $a=0$, set $U=v$, $V=bu+cv$; then $q=UV$ and the inverse substitution is $v=U$, $u=(V-cU)/b$. If $a\ne0$, set $r_2=-b/a-r$. From $p(r)=0$ obtain $q=a(u-rv)(u-r_2v)$ and $\Delta=a^2(r-r_2)^2$, so $r\ne r_2$. Set $U=a(u-rv)$ and $V=u-r_2v$. Their inverse is $v=(U/a-V)/(r_2-r)$, $u=V+r_2v$. Substitution and its displayed inverse define inverse continuous $K$-algebra maps on the two-variable power series rings: in every fixed total degree only finitely many terms contribute, so these identities hold coefficientwise. They carry $q$ to $UV$ and hence identify $K[[u,v]]/(q)$ with $K[[U,V]]/(UV)$. This is the concrete split-form calculation behind Tag 0CBU; it requires no extraction of a square root or division by two.

source.place: Tag 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), condition (2), explicit linear change of coordinates

proof.text: Let $x'$ be the canonical $K$-rational lift of $z$ in $D_K=C_K$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $z$ in $D$; the evaluation map $S\to F$ has a maximal kernel $\mathfrak p$, and $S_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{D,z}$ with residue field $F$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] with ground field $F$, residue extension $F/F$, and extension field $K/F$. Its clause for every presentation applies with $n=2$, the single relation $q$, and the presentation of step 5; here the coefficient-field section is just the structural $F$-map. The kernel $\mathfrak q$ of $S\otimes_FK\to K$ is exactly the point $x'$ by construction. The node gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_K,x'}\cong K[[u,v]]/(q)$ as $K$-algebras. Compose with step 7 to obtain $K[[U,V]]/(UV)$. Its residue-field clause gives $K\to\kappa(x')$ an isomorphism, and $x'$ lies over $x$. Finally [lem-zl-separable-permanence] applied to $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ proves $K/k$ separable. The products of a finite $k$-basis of $F$ with a basis of $K/F$ span $K$ over $k$, so $K/k$ is finite. Take $k'=K$, containing the chosen copy $\kappa(x)=F$, with $[k':\kappa(x)]\le2$.
